html:
The Qhara Qhara were an Aymara-speaking people and lordship of the southern Bolivian highlands, in today's Potosí and Chuquisaca, centred on Macha. With the Charka they formed one of the largest confederations among the Aymara kingdoms.

Under the Inca they served as soldiers. The great silver mountain of Potosí stood on their land, and after 1545 the Spanish drew forced labour for its mines from them through the mit'a, a labour draft adapted from Inca practice. In 1582 their lords joined in writing the Memorial de Charcas to defend their rank and rights. Today the Qhara Qhara Nation, a council of ayllus (kin communities), works for self-rule within plurinational Bolivia.
